slides.title: Belgium — accommodation path
bullets: Recognised diversity instead of denying it.
Equal Dutch–French ministers in central government.

slides.title: Belgium's COMMUNITY GOVERNMENT
bullets: Elected by people of one language community.
A unique 4th tier — beyond centre / state / local.

slides.title: Did it work?
bullets: Avoided civic strife between the two communities.
Country stayed together; no division on linguistic lines.
Brussels — chosen as headquarters of EU.
Belgian model is COMPLEX but effective.
Sri Lanka is recovering from a quarter-century war.

slides.title: Why share power? — Prudential reason
bullets: Imposing the majority looks easy short-term.
Tyranny of majority hurts majority too.

slides.title: Why share power? — Moral reason
bullets: Power-sharing is the very SPIRIT of democracy.
People have right to be CONSULTED.
A legitimate government — citizens have a stake.

slides.title: Form 1 — HORIZONTAL distribution
bullets: Same level — each can check the others.
E.g. Supreme Court strikes down a law.

slides.title: Form 2 — VERTICAL distribution
bullets: Not done in Sri Lanka — denied.

slides.title: Form 3 — SOCIAL GROUPS
bullets: Power shared across linguistic / religious groups.
RESERVED CONSTITUENCIES for SC, ST, women in India.
Gives minorities a fair share in power.

slides.title: Form 4 — PARTIES + PRESSURE GROUPS
bullets: COALITION governments share power between parties.
Power doesn't stay in one hand.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Belgium accommodated diversity; Sri Lanka chose majoritarianism — and civil war.
Belgium: equal ministers + state govts + Brussels deal + community govt.
Sri Lanka: Sinhala-only language + pro-Buddhism + denied autonomy.
Two reasons for power-sharing: prudential + moral.
Four forms: horizontal, vertical, social-group, parties.
In a democracy, power MUST be distributed among as many citizens as possible.
